$comment: ALLOWLIST SEMANTICS: an SPDX id that appears in no list below is PROHIBITED.
A new licence string must be classified by a human before it can ship.
Owner: QA & Security Engineer. Changes to this file require security review.

server.description: Next.js server, parser worker, database layer. Not distributed to users, so most copyleft triggers do not fire.
server.classifiedBy: not present in the bundler client module list

client.description: Anything the bundler emits into JavaScript sent to the browser. THIS IS DISTRIBUTION, to every visitor. All attribution and source-availability obligations fire here.
client.classifiedBy: bundler client module list, never by package.json position

permitted.$comment: Plan section 3.2 - permissive, no condition beyond attribution. Allowed on server and client.
standingObligations: Preserve copyright notices and licence text (discharged by generated THIRD-PARTY-LICENCES.md, plan section 3.6).
Apache-2.0 only: carry forward upstream NOTICE file content. Apache-2.0 section 4 requires it and it is the most commonly missed attribution obligation.

conditional.$comment: Plan section 3.3 - weak copyleft. Permitted with conditions; note the per-licence surface restriction.

MPL-2.0.reason: MPL-2.0 section 3.3 explicitly permits combining MPL files with proprietary code into a Larger Work. This is the case MPL was written for.
conditions: Unmodified only: never fork, vendor-patch, or inline an MPL dependency.
Any modification we make to an MPL-covered file must itself be released under MPL-2.0. If a patch is unavoidable, upstream it or publish the patched file.
MPL-2.0.enforcement: CI records the obligation; the unmodified-only discipline is a code review rule.

EPL-2.0.reason: Weak copyleft; permits combination with proprietary code in a Larger Work. The secondary-licence provision grants recipients a GPL-2.0 option, which is a right granted to them, not an obligation on us.
conditions: PREFERENCE, not prohibition: choose a permissive alternative of comparable quality when one exists. EPL carries more litigation-and-patent text than MPL and is less familiar to reviewers.
EPL-2.0.knownInstance: elkjs is EPL-2.0 and is client-bundled, therefore distributed. See plan section 3.5.

CDDL-1.0.reason: File-level copyleft; server-side only as a precaution.

CDDL-1.1.reason: File-level copyleft; server-side only as a precaution.

WTFPL.reason: Permissive in intent, legally sloppy. Allowed only by recorded exception in licence-exceptions.json, and preferably replaced.

lgplClientProhibition.$comment: Stated once so the gate and the reviewer read the same sentence.
lgplClientProhibition.rule: LGPL of any version MUST NOT enter the client bundle.
lgplClientProhibition.reason: Bundlers perform what is effectively static linking, which triggers LGPL's relinking obligations (LGPL-3.0 section 4) and means shipping object files or equivalent so a user can substitute their own version. Server-side, where nothing is distributed, LGPL is unproblematic.

prohibited.$comment: Plan section 3.4. Prohibited on every surface, including transitively.

entries.reason: Network use triggers the source obligation for the ENTIRE combined work. This is the one that could force us to publish Diagram Mapper.
entries.note: Hard prohibition, no exceptions, including transitive. Running an AGPL tool as a separate program in CI (for example trufflehog) is not linking and is out of scope of this prohibition.

entries.reason: Strong copyleft over the combined work; the mere-aggregation argument is too thin to rest a business on.
Requires releasing the source of the entire service stack if offered as a service. Aimed precisely at us.
Restrict commercial or hosted use OF THE DEPENDENCY. Note the asymmetry: BUSL-1.1 is a fine licence for OUR code and an unacceptable one for a dependency.
Non-commercial or no-derivatives. Incompatible with selling a product.
entries.note: Applies to the asset manifest (fonts, icons, images) as much as to package.json. CC-BY-4.0 without NC/ND is permitted with attribution; see assets.

entries.reason: The 'shall be used for Good, not Evil' clause is unenforceably vague and a known blocker for commercial use. A documented reason to avoid org.json-lineage packages.

unresolved.$comment: Plan section 3.4, final row. Unknown is NOT permissive.
unresolved.treatment: prohibited until a human resolves it
unresolved.resolution: Read the upstream repository, then either (a) record the finding in licence-exceptions.json with the actual SPDX id and a source URL, or (b) remove the dependency.

assets.$comment: Plan section 3.5. Fonts, icon sets and images are dependencies too and are routinely missed because they are not in package.json.
assets.rule: Every font, icon set and image gets an SPDX id and a source URL recorded before it is committed. The CI gate covers the asset manifest as well as package.json.
knownTraps: Font Awesome Free mixes CC-BY-4.0 (icons, attribution required) with MIT (code).
Many icon sets are CC-BY-4.0 and the attribution is mandatory, not courteous.
Some commercial fonts forbid web embedding outright regardless of purchase.

attribution.reason: Committed output means a licence change in a dependency shows up as a reviewable diff rather than as a surprise.

failsBuildOn: any unknown, missing or unparseable licence
any conditional licence appearing on a surface the policy does not permit for it (notably LGPL in the client bundle)
any asset in the manifest without an SPDX id and source URL
deliberatelyAvoided: hosted licence-compliance services (paid; CEO escalation required before any purchase)
